comments.text: The tropics overall are a poorer region than the north and south temperate zones. The tropics usually have poorer soil compared to the temperate zones. There is also more competition for resources from other organisms, which harms agricultural output. The tropics are a more challenging place to build a strong diversified economy. Africa is the most tropical continent on Earth with around 80% of it's land within the tropics. Not surprisingly, the most developed areas in Africa have been in temperate North Africa and temperate South Africa. In this interglacial period, the middle latitudes reign supreme.

replies.author: @pteranodon6612
replies.text: ​@ASzw-d4j Most of the places you mentioned are in the temperate zone and don't have many of the problems I mentioned earlier. The only example you gave that's in the tropics is Southeast Asia which has trailed behind temperate Northeast Asia in economic development.  It's not really the "cold" countries that do the best (like Iceland and Greenland), but the temperate countries that cycle between warm and cold. These are mostly at the middle latitudes. You can see this with Canada, which is highly productive in the extreme south of the country where there's a temperate climate, but that productivity drops sharply as you go north into subarctic and arctic climates. This is mostly related to agriculture.
